corridors.name: Portland to Hood River — Columbia Gorge end to end
corridors.reason: Long Columbia Gorge control route; the route should stay on ordinary roads without needing I-84, while its long length is deliberately paired with a short-hop check in the verification report.

corridors.name: Viento State Park to Hood River — Gorge trail pinch point
corridors.reason: Short hop across the Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail / Mitchell Point area; nominated to expose a local trail seam that a Portland-to-Hood-River detour could absorb.

corridors.name: Astoria to Seaside — north coast control
corridors.reason: Coastal US 101 corridor, testing north-coast linework and the state highway data where the route is not an inland metro shortcut.

corridors.name: Corvallis to Newport — Willamette Valley to coast
corridors.reason: Long valley-to-coast control through a distinct terrain and road-network transition; checks that the route does not fall onto a freeway-only connection.

corridors.name: Medford to Ashland — southern Oregon control
corridors.reason: Southern Oregon urban corridor parallel to I-5; tests ordinary-road connectivity and functional-class coverage near a major interstate.
